assertions.name: no_unrecognised_crossing_shift
assertions.source: every stored d is exactly 0, -h or -h/2 -- compared as mpf, not via str(): the str round-trip truncates to ~17 digits and would put all 22 in 'other'

assertions.name: code_proton_is_eleven
assertions.source: hecke_core proton = 11 crossings, matching the derivation (bare 9 = 6 B_3 + 3 quark, plus one Hopf link = 2 gluon)

assertions.name: code_proton_decomposition_matches_the_c5_block
assertions.source: c5-involution-leibniz-decomposition-interpretation.md:18 says '7 pure sigma_0, 4 pure sigma_1, 1 averaged sigma_0, 1 averaged sigma_1, 3 inverted sigma_1^-1' -- gen0=7 (6 pure + 1 averaged), gen1=4 (3 inverted + 1 averaged). The code matches EXACTLY, so that block describes the LONG model faithfully

assertions.name: THE_CONTRADICTION_neutron_derived_13_implemented_11
assertions.source: the corpus derives 13 crossings for the neutron (two Hopf links, 4 gluon crossings, because the dd crossing is a deeper instability: tr_M = -0.132 vs -0.006) while hecke_core implements 11. Delta_L = neutron - proton is built on the 11. NOT adjudicated here

assertions.name: the_citation_does_not_say_what_it_is_cited_for
assertions.source: q-beta-gamma-gamma-canonical-derivation.md:33 cites def:categorical-proton and def:categorical-neutron as authority for '11 typed crossings each'. That is right for the proton and wrong for the neutron: the neutron definition's own properties block derives 13. Same stale-citation class as the convention-C citations drained in this branch

description: qou-bg3w: categorical-neutron-properties derives a 13-crossing neutron (6 B_3 + 3 quark + 4 gluon, two Hopf links) while q-beta-gamma-gamma-canonical-derivation asserts 11 for both nucleons -- citing the very definition that derives 13 -- and hecke_core implements 11. The proton is consistent at 11 across all three. Scope-(a): establishes the mismatch, adjudicates nothing, changes no compute.
